requirement: The book preprocessor MUST escape requirement names and link targets when inserting badge HTML. It MUST encode badge label and message text in Shields.io URL path components so punctuation cannot change the badge URL structure.
rationale:
The tests adequately check `requirements.references.safe_badges`. I derived two obligations from the requirement text.

**Obligation 1: escape requirement names and link targets when inserting badge HTML.** Two sites insert such HTML: `replace_definitions` (the definition header badges) and `reference_badge` (reference badges). Both are covered.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definition_evidence_link_targets_are_escaped]` gives the index chapter a rendered path containing `&`, `"`, `<` and `>`. It asserts the exact escaped `href` of the name badge, `a&b "q" <x>/rules.ready.html`. It also asserts the raw `a&b`, `"q"` and `<x>` forms are absent. This covers the definition-header link target.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reference_link_targets_are_escaped]` gives the target chapter a rendered path containing the same special characters. It asserts the exact escaped `href` of a `{cite}` badge, `a&b "q" <x>.html#habeas-req-rules.ready`. It also asserts the raw special characters are absent. This covers the reference-badge link target.
- Requirement names can't contain HTML-special characters. `valid_name` only admits ASCII alphanumerics, `_` and `-`. The link-target tests, with special characters in the path, therefore exercise the only meaningful escaping distinction. The badge `alt` text is escaped and tested in the shield tests below.

**Obligation 2: percent-encode badge label and message text in Shields.io URL path components so punctuation cannot change the URL structure.**
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[badge_urls_percent_encode_punctuation_and_html_is_escaped]` calls `shield_badge` with `/`, `?`, `#`, `%`, `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`, a space and a non-ASCII `é`. It asserts the exact `src` URL: `a%2Fb%3Fc-x%23y%25z%26w%3Cv%3E%22u%27_caf%C3%A9-006ba8?style=flat-square&labelColor=555`. It also asserts the exact HTML-escaped `alt` text. Together these show each structural punctuation character is encoded and the URL's query part is unchanged.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[shields_badge_urls_escape_requirement_names]` covers the Shields-specific `_` → `__` and `-` → `--` doubling, and a space → `_` in the message. These are the cases where a literal separator would otherwise change the badge's label/message split. It asserts both the URL and the `alt` text.

**Gaps.** I found none. Every clause has a test with a concrete assertion on the output, and the assertions match the requirement's expected behavior. No `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply.
